plain_english_title: Respiratory System Regulations (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97): Breathing Tests, Sinusitis/Rhinitis, Asthma & Sleep Apnea
what_this_means: Effective October 7, 1996 (61 FR 46720), VA modernized its respiratory rating schedule (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97) around objective Pulmonary Function Test (PFT) numbers (FEV-1, FEV-1/FVC, FVC, and DLCO diffusing capacity), inhaler/steroid medication tiers for Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602), dedicated formulas for Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) and Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522), and Sleep Apnea Syndromes (Diagnostic Code 6847, awarding 50% when a CPAP or breathing assistance device is medically required)—followed on October 6, 2006 (71 FR 52457) by § 4.96(d)'s rules on when PFTs can be excused and which PFT score governs. Crucially, § 4.96(a) prevents combining multiple LOWER-respiratory codes (Diagnostic Codes 6600–6817 and 6822–6847), while leaving UPPER-respiratory nose and sinus codes (Diagnostic Codes 6502–6524) completely separate to combine!
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet that improperly folded upper-respiratory Chronic Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) or Allergic Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522) into a lower-respiratory Asthma or Sleep Apnea rating—violating the plain numeric boundaries of 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a).

Coexisting service-connected Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602) and Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847) rated flatly at 50% without evaluating whether combined lower-respiratory severity warrants elevation to the next higher tier (60% or 100%) under § 4.96(a).

Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602) rated at 10% despite daily use of an inhaled anti-inflammatory corticosteroid or daily bronchodilator (which meets the 30% tier), or rated at 30% despite three or more courses per year of oral/injectable systemic steroids (which meets the 60% tier).

A respiratory cancer (Diagnostic Code 6819, a PACT Act presumptive condition) reduced from 100% after treatment without a mandatory VA examination 6 months after treatment ended and 60 days' advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e).
important_cautions: Lower-respiratory non-combination rule (§ 4.96(a)): VA cannot assign separate stacked percentages for two lower-respiratory conditions within Diagnostic Codes 6600–6817 and 6822–6847 (for example, Asthma + COPD + Sleep Apnea); instead, VA assigns one rating under the predominant code with potential elevation to the next higher tier.

October 7, 1996 and October 6, 2006 date gates: Diagnostic Code 6847 (50% CPAP Sleep Apnea) and modern FEV-1/DLCO tables took effect October 7, 1996 (published September 5, 1996 at 61 FR 46720), while § 4.96(d) PFT rules (including § 4.96(d)(7), barring compensable ratings from FEV-1/FVC ratio alone when both FEV-1 and FVC exceed 100% predicted) took effect October 6, 2006—neither can establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) before its effective date.

Sleep apnea CPAP rules have NOT changed: VA's February 15, 2022 proposed rule and September 12, 2024 supplemental notice (RIN 2900-AQ72, 87 FR 8474 & 89 FR 74162) remain proposed and unfinalized (not enacted law); the 50% CPAP rule under Diagnostic Code 6847 remains binding law.
Remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c): once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion on a specific Board issue, no further CUE motions are permitted on that issue.
questions_for_representative: Did VA keep my upper-respiratory Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) and Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522—30% with nasal polyps, 10% without polyps with >50% obstruction) separate from my lower-respiratory Asthma or Sleep Apnea rating?

On my Pulmonary Function Test report, if FEV-1%, FEV-1/FVC, and DLCO (SB) pointed to different rating levels, did the examiner explain which test best reflects my disability under 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)(6)?
Do my pharmacy records show daily inhaled corticosteroids/bronchodilators (30%) or three or more annual systemic steroid courses (60%) under Diagnostic Code 6602?
If I have both Sleep Apnea and Asthma/COPD, did VA evaluate elevation to the next higher percentage tier under 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)?
